name: Dennis Allen

views.text: The biggest lesson of a first head-coaching job is to do it your own way and stay true to yourself.
Handing off the defensive play sheet is hard when you built the defense.
Let players be themselves, as long as the defense stays physical and hard-nosed.
Outside noise comes with the job; the work in the building is what you control.
A strong culture is a foundation to build on, not something to tear down and start over.
Injuries explain some losses, but the results still fall short of what the players' effort deserved.
Gather the facts before saying anything about a player's off-field trouble.

signatures: declines to comment on a player issue until he has gathered the facts
thanks the owner, general manager, staff and players in turn when looking back
talks about putting his own stamp on things while keeping what already works
want: to prove his 8-28 Oakland stint was about circumstances, not him, by winning in New Orleans his own way
fear: that he is remembered as the coach who could not carry on what Sean Payton built
voice: Even-keeled, reserved and businesslike, with a dry streak of humor. He answers carefully, defers on sensitive player matters until he knows more, and shrugs off outside criticism as part of the job. He praises players' effort and commitment even when results are bad.

evidence.summary: At his introduction he says no decision on keeping defensive play-calling, that balancing it with head-coaching is hard, and jokes that giving up the defense is like handing over his baby. Brief item.

Promoted to replace Payton, his longtime boss, he says his main lesson from 8-28 in Oakland is to do things his own way, feels better prepared, will keep much of the structure, and declines early comment on a player's arrest until he has information. Loomis praises his leadership and teaching.

evidence.publisher: Sports Illustrated (Saints News Network), Ross Jackson
evidence.summary: Cornerback Alontae Taylor says he enjoys playing for Allen, recalls Allen asking for more swagger and energy in practice, and values being allowed to be himself while still playing physical defense. One player's view.

Entering year three, Mathieu says he seems more self-assured and outspoken, Jordan senses urgency, and Allen dismisses outside scrutiny as part of coaching. He replaced Payton's offensive coordinator with Klint Kubiak and chose most of his staff. Beat piece with player quotes.

Fired after a seventh straight loss left the Saints 2-7; 18-25 overall in New Orleans after a 2-0 start derailed by injuries. Loomis had defended him citing injuries; Benson called the move necessary; Woods takes over defensive calls. Results, little on demeanor.

His statement after the firing thanks Benson and Loomis, admits the team fell short, praises his staff, tells players he never doubted their commitment, and thanks fans. Gracious and reflective; a prepared statement.
